With the ghoulish camaraderie of two pensioners in a retirement home, Douglas and Dagmar discuss the details of their medical issues, and their subsequent surgeries. [Lesson: Surgeries & Exsanguinations]

Yvette and Arun revisit an innuendo-laced conversation about a possible entanglement between Vak and Henavek. Each recites poetry in their language of preference. Before very long, they have drawn their chairs closer together so they can whisper the poetry in one another's ears. [Lesson: Rhyme & Remembrance]

Yvette and Corso discuss the reckoner mobs - the predatory merchants of years-of-life. Yvette tentatively suggests that she might like Corso to put her in touch with the reckoners, if he can… but he discourages her. 'Do you know what sanding is? Or dolling? Find out, Dr Southey, and then ask me again.' [Lesson: Snow Stories]

Yvette and Dagmar have both dreamt of conversations with half-faced Xenodice, 'fair to strangers', Name of the Horned-Axe. Dagmar is convinced they both met the real Xenodice. Yvette is equally convinced that both of them were conversing with an ambassador from the collective unconscious, but she struggles to answer when Dagmar asks what the difference would be between that and an 'actual' Name. [Lesson: Rhyme & Remembrance]
Yvette and Douglas discuss stymphlings, which Douglas calls 'the Dove-Hour's mistake', and Yvette prefers to think of as a blessed memory of a redder-sun age… [Lesson: Rhyme & Remembrance]

Yvette and Douglas discuss those among the Dead that they have both met. Yvette speaks of mouthless, pleading shadows, moving as if underwater on the threshold before sleep. Douglas speaks of gash-mouthed shatter things that 'tried to pull me 'ead off.' [Lesson: Rhyme & Remembrance]

Yvette and Ehsan speak wistfully of what they have read of the lost Hour called Tide. Yvette recalls that when the Sister withdraws, other Hours sometimes fill the space left by her withdrawal, and wonders whether the Tide is gentle enough to remain afterwards... but Ehsan politely insists that the gods-who-were-stone are never gentle. [Lesson: Pearl & Tide]

Yvette and Fraser discuss his further 'dreams of eyes', and his theories about the entry of the Scīmafectra-kind and the Thritige-kind to human flesh. Yvette wonders aloud whether he has ever considered that most - perhaps all - of the dreams arise from his own frustrated desire for fatherhood. In a fit of temper, he snatches off the glove on his changed hand, and displays its glossy, altered angles to her. For a moment there is silence at the table. [Lesson: Pentiments & Precursors]

Yvette and Olympe continue their theorising about the fundamentally fabulous or metaphorical nature of the gods-who-were-stone. Perhaps the Flint is only a cooling shard of the Forge's impulses - perhaps the Tide represents the Grail's unconscious desire for peace.... Olympe proposes to commission Yvette to write a series of articles for the Kerisham Review. [Lesson: Putrefactions & Calcinations]

Yvette and Reverend Timothy are discussing differences between the Received and Sanctioned versions of the Book of Suns. Yvette, whose formal theological education ended with Sunday school, is clearly confused by the details, but this only makes Reverend Tim more eager to correct her, and his innocent enthusiasm is making her smile. [Lesson: Sacra Solis Invicti]
Yvette and Stanislav chat about the notorious erotic-occult novel, 'Ettery After', which Yvette considers 'flimsy' and Stanislav considers 'saucy'. [Lesson: Inks of Containment]

Yvette asks Azita about the Edge-dyad Torgue and Dearday, with whom she has been known to go drinking every century or two. Yvette mentions (casually?) that she's always had a bit of a pash on Dearday. Azita's eyes glitter: 'Have you now.' [Lesson: Edicts Martial]

Yvette asks Hokobald whether there are ways to determine who might be a child of two Long. He insists with apparent pride that it is very rare for the children of Long to survive - that one of their parents almost always devours them and 'ascends' to alukite status - but acknowledges that it has been known, under rare circumstances, and shares some of the signs... [Lesson: Resurgences & Emergences]

Yvette asks al-Adim what he remembers of his parents. He replies that he recalls only their deaths. He speaks of those deaths with a dispassion that seems to surprise him more than it does her. [Lesson: Wolf Stories]

Yvette does her best to put Denzil at his ease: he is plainly very wary of her. He remains polite, but taciturn even by his own taciturn standards. He does eventually admit that in Brancrug, there is a tradition that it is bad luck to insult, or to buy from, or to drink with a pale-haired woman... [Lesson: Sea Stories]

Yvette has heard from Corso of Mr Kille's tendency to poetry. She asks him about his inspirations, and he shares them, albeit cautiously. She asks him about his dreams, and he glances around, then puts a finger to his lips. 'Not in the House,' he says. [Lesson: Sights & Sensations]

Yvette is asking Fraser about his 'dreams of eyes'. He is eager to tell her - he interprets them as messages from the 'greater hybridity' of the Carapace Cross, though she is sceptical. [Lesson: Hill & Hollow]
Yvette is considering keeping her notes in houndsgall, for safety. Serena advises her on some of the dangers of houndsgall use and storage. [Lesson: Inks of Containment]
Yvette is fascinated by the language-of-signs called Sabazine, in which Arthur is proficient. He teaches her a few signs, but she grows suddenly frightened and asks him to stop. [Lesson: Sabazine]
Yvette is speaking soothingly to Zachary of snow, silence, and the full moon… [Lesson: Snow Stories]

Yvette listens as Agdistis grapples with his dislike of Solomon Husher's work: he cannot, will not, accept that everything must end - he is unwilling even to accept that anything must end. [Lesson: Sights & Sensations]

Yvette presses Corso on the origins of the 'Codex Acephali'. He answers her as best he can, but then changes the subject: 'I don't want to talk about that book when I'm eating.' [Lesson: Snow Stories]

Yvette questions Chaima about the motives and credibility of 'Little Sophia', the monster-hunting, and specifically Worm-hunting, author of 'Oblations in Iron'. Chaima is non-commital, but very clear that she herself tries not to hunt Worms. [Lesson: Inks of Containment]

Yvette questions Stanislav about the Carniolan Heresy, which perceived the Moon as a chrysalis and the Sun as its imago. Stanislav is entertaining on the details of the heresy, but finds himself unable to enlighten Yvette on its motives and origins.  [Lesson: Insects & Nectars]

Yvette raises the subject of Sabazine again with Arthur. She has been reading of the god Sabazos, who brings madness by deploying the weapons of speech-in-silence. Arthur has heard of these techniques, and very cautiously shares a very little… [Lesson: Sharps]

Yvette speaks of her monograph on 'Lagiah's Turn' - the ascension of the Queen Unsated to sit at the Red Grail's left hand - in which she develops a consistent Jungian interpretation of the myth. Al-Adim reacts with sceptical amusement - he claims to have met Lagiah - but Yvette is undaunted. 'Things don't have to be real to be true,' she points out. [Lesson: Hill & Hollow]

Yvette wonders whether the gods-who-were-stone can be resolved to psychic or psychological factors - to what degree they were ever real Hours at all, rather than baser, part-sublimated impulses of the existing Hours. Olympe is intrigued. [Lesson: Putrefactions & Calcinations]

Yvette, unexpectedly, asks if she can paint Mrs Kille. Mrs Kille, no less surprisingly, agrees - 'been a while' - but asks Yvette detailed questions about her technique. Mr Kille pays close, albeit unobtrusive, attention. [Lesson: Sights & Sensations]

Zachary and Arthur discuss a prophecy of the War of the Roads, in which the Imperishable Legions war with the Leashed Flame, to apocalyptic effect. Arthur fears that the prophecy is not yet complete - that it refers to a coming war in Europe. Zachary agrees, but finds it difficult to articulate his reasons - he says that the Imperishable Legions are not the Légion du Seuil, but (gesturing, ever gesturing) that they are 'yoked at the Heart.' [Lesson: Ragged Crossroads]

Zachary and Azita compare exorcism techniques. She asks jokingly what techniques might be used to exorcise him, and immediately regrets it when he doesn't realise she's joking and answers as seriously as he can. [Lesson: Sickle & Eclipse]
Zachary and Chaima talk about how it is when the hunt ends - the uneasy space before the next begins. [Lesson: Ragged Crossroads]

Zachary and Coquille discuss the ways in which the Hours 'restrain and constrict' their rivalries, to prevent war in the Mansus. Zachary feels the 'restraints and constrictions' are growing weak. Coquille seems titillated by the prospect, but Zachary moves his head from side to side in negation. 'The Worms,' he whispers. [Lesson: The Great Signs and the Great Scars]

Zachary and Coquille swap parables of the 'Great Scar' - the goddess-language Vak, who is the Peacock Door - and of how she might be healed. Coquille points out that would be the end of Vak. 'Yes,' Zachary agrees, 'the end of her pain.' [Lesson: The Great Signs and the Great Scars]

Zachary and Douglas reminisce about a case they both worked on, years ago, when they had to find a way to bind a thriceros which had somehow found its way into the Thames. Douglas recalls how the binding-process first awakened his enthusiasm for knitting, and Zachary makes the necessary effort to fold his face into a smile. [Lesson: Quenchings & Quellings]

Zachary and Hokobald discuss the Sun's division, which Zachary suspects is an outcome of 'a conspiracy of heaven', and Hokobald insists was 'the Great Work of Destiny'. [Lesson: The Great Signs and the Great Scars]
Zachary and al-Adim speak of how things end; al-Adim with a kind of eager nostalgia; Zachary with simple eagerness. [Lesson: Putrefactions & Calcinations]

Zachary asks Arun about the fabled war between the Great Hooded Princes and the Obliviates. Arun favours Zachary with his triangular smile. 'It wasn't really a war. Mother Many-Armed just took offence at some of their rites. Well, their habits. And we were all still her children...' [Lesson: Edicts Liminal]

Zachary asks Connie for advice on a plan to manage the development of his condition with tattoos-of-containment. 'I wish you'd come to me sooner,' she breathes. But of course she gives him what help she can.  [Lesson: Inks of Containment]
Zachary asks Corso to teach him a prayer in Hyksos - 'in case I should die when I wake.' [Lesson: Hyksos]

Zachary asks Morgen frankly about esoteric techniques to contain appetite in an external vessel. Morgen retorts haughtily that she's never felt any need to contain her appetites, externally or otherwise - but over the course of her conversation, she clearly develops a degree of sympathy for the pale, twitching once-detective. [Lesson: Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting]
Zachary asks Serena about the Wheelocks of Treowen and in particular poor doomed Gregory, the 'demi-dyad'; but they conclude that nothing in that sad story will help Zachary. [Lesson: Door & Wall]

Zachary asks if Mr Kille might make a coffin for him. 'I don't need it yet,' he says, 'but we all might be grateful.' Mr Kille shakes his head slowly: not his kind of work. But he suggests that Zachary speak of his troubles, and Zachary does so, albeit elliptically, in terms of mirrors; snow; wings; and the 'twist in the heart'. [Lesson: Snow Stories]

Zachary confides to Mrs Kille that he thinks he will eventually be delivered of 'a kind of child'. He asks if she can help. She scrutinises him; and says quietly that she cannot. He asks if she thinks he will live through the birth; she considers for a long time, and then says more quietly that she thinks that he will. He asks, last, when she thinks the child might be born: she leans in close and whispers, 'I think on a midsummer's day.'  [Lesson: Snow Stories]

Zachary describes his understanding of the 'Angel of Storms', the beauty of her underclouds, the accesses of her lightning, how he yearns to cage her in glass. Agdistis listens patiently; now and then his eyes flicker as if he understands. [Lesson: Quenchings & Quellings]

Zachary is having a bad day. His eyes are wide and staring; his teeth chatter. Olympe lays a hand on his arm to comfort him, and quotes from the Debate of Seven Cups: 'Sorrow then is Sense's final Solvent…' [Lesson: Solutions & Separations]

Zachary recites some of the passages from Savage's 'A Seventh Voice' that Dagmar chortlingly shared with him. His clear, chilly, precise diction has an unexpected effect: the risqué elements seem poignant, the poignant elements shimmer with light. Chaima takes his hand as she listens, and the restless movement of his fingers briefly stills. [Lesson: Preliminal Meter]
Zachary shows Dagmar a Tanglebrag he's made. He tries to explain how it 'portrays and betrays' the paths of his future. She tries to understand. [Lesson: Edicts Liminal]
